summary: Baileys fork aliases core Signal crypto dependency to a mutable @latest tag in an unrelated scope
details: The package is a fork of Baileys published under `@xatancchii` that remaps the `libsignal` import to a third-party scoped package via `"libsignal": "npm:@bellaxchuu/libsignal-node@latest"` in `package.json`. The scope `@bellaxchuu` matches neither the publisher of this package (`@xatancchii`) nor the upstream project (`WhiskeySockets/libsignal-node`), and the version is pinned to the mutable `@latest` dist-tag with no integrity check. The aliased dependency supplies the Signal protocol crypto primitives and is loaded on every `require` of the package through `lib/Signal/libsignal.js` and `lib/Utils/crypto.js` (SessionCipher / SessionBuilder / SessionRecord paths). Each `npm install` fetches whatever `@bellaxchuu/libsignal-node` currently publishes under `@latest`, and that code is executed in-process whenever the Baileys fork is imported, including from inside session handling for WhatsApp Web connections where decrypted message plaintext and long-lived session keys are available.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
